Series::index_put¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signatures¶

Series::index_put(pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<Series> indices, const Series& values, bool accumulate) const -> Series
Series::index_put(std::initializer_list<Series> indices, const Series& values, bool accumulate) const -> Series
Series::index_put(std::int64_t index, const Series& values) const -> Series

What It Does¶

Returns a modified copy after writing through explicit index tensors.

This is the copy-returning sibling of index_put_():

  • index_put_() mutates the existing series

  • index_put() leaves the original alone and returns the patched copy

The overload split matters because the family actually covers two different styles of write:

  • general advanced-index writes through Series index tensors

  • a narrow 1D scalar convenience overload

The general overloads are richer than the current signature alone suggests. They support:

  • integer position tensors

  • bool masks

  • scalar replacement

  • one-value-per-selected-head updates

  • trailing-slice pattern reuse

  • additive updates through accumulate=true

Unlike index_put_(), this copy-returning family does not provide an ExtractSpec convenience overload. If you want selector-language copy-returning writes, use extract_put().

Parameters¶

indices (pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<Series> or std::initializer_list<Series>)

The explicit index tensors for the general overloads.

These can be:

  • integer index tensors

  • bool masks

  • undefined entries when routed through lower-level mixed-index machinery

The initializer-list form is the most convenient when the index tensors are spelled inline. The RangeView form is the right choice when the index list already lives in a container.

index (std::int64_t)

The scalar convenience form.

This overload is intentionally narrow: it patches one logical position in a 1D series and expects a scalar values source.

values (const Series&)

The replacement data.

For the general overloads, the accepted cardinality depends on the indexed shape:

  • scalar: one value reused everywhere

  • one value per selected advanced head

  • one full tail pattern reused across every selected head

  • one fully expanded output block

For the scalar convenience form, values must be scalar.

accumulate (bool)

Only present on the general overloads.

  • false: replacement semantics

  • true: additive semantics

Returns¶

Series A new series containing the requested updates.

Note

One-dimensional single-integer-list writes use the flat fast path If you call index_put({idx}, values, ...) on a 1D series with one integer index tensor, the public API intentionally reuses the same flat write semantics as put_(): duplicate integer indices with accumulate=false keep last-write behavior rather than rejecting the overlap.

Examples¶

Example 1. The initializer-list overload is the shortest copy-returning form for a basic integer index write.

auto vec = pluss::make_series(std::vector<double>{0, 1, 2, 3, 4}, {5});
auto idx = pluss::make_series(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 3}, {2});
auto picked = pluss::make_series(std::vector<double>{90, 70}, {2});

std::cout << vec.index_put({idx}, picked, false);

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 90, 2, 70, 4]

Example 2. Because this is the copy-returning family, the original source series is unchanged.

std::cout << vec;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]

Example 3. The RangeView overload is useful when the index list already lives in a container, and accumulate=true turns the update into an additive write.

auto overlap_idx = pluss::make_series(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 1, 3}, {3});
auto overlap_values = pluss::make_series(std::vector<double>{10, 20, 30}, {3});
std::vector<pluss::Series> overlap_indices{overlap_idx};

std::cout << vec.index_put(
    pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<pluss::Series>(overlap_indices),
    overlap_values,
    true);

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 31, 2, 33, 4]

Example 4. A bool mask write is also part of the general overload family.

auto mask = pluss::make_series(std::vector<bool>{false, true, false, true, false}, {5});
std::cout << vec.index_put({mask}, pluss::codem::value(-1.0), false);

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[0, -1, 2, -1, 4]

The bool mask selects positions 1 and 3, and the scalar replacement is reused for both.

Example 5. A non-indexed trailing slice can be supplied once and reused across every selected head.

auto mat = pluss::make_series(
    std::vector<double>{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9},
    {3, 3});
auto row_idx = pluss::make_series(std::vector<std::int64_t>{0, 2}, {2});
auto tail_pattern = pluss::make_series(std::vector<double>{100, 200, 300}, {3});

std::cout << mat.index_put({row_idx}, tail_pattern, false);

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=9, contiguous=true)
data=[[100, 200, 300],
  [4, 5, 6],
  [100, 200, 300]]

This is a good example of the “tail pattern” cardinality mode: the same length-3 row is reused for each selected row index.

Example 6. The scalar convenience overload targets one 1D position, and negative indices count from the end.

std::cout << vec.index_put(-1, pluss::codem::value(555.0));

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 1, 2, 3, 555]

Example 7. On the 1D single-integer-list path, duplicate indices with accumulate=false keep last-write semantics.

std::cout << vec.index_put({overlap_idx}, overlap_values, false);

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 20, 2, 30, 4]

That is the same replace-vs-last-write behavior as put_(), because this specific public shape reuses the 1D flat write route.

Notes¶

  • index_put() is the copy-returning explicit-index write family.

  • Bool masks are part of the general overload semantics.

  • The values cardinality rules are richer than “scalar or exact output match”; trailing-slice reuse is also supported.

  • If you want the original object mutated, use index_put_().

See Also¶

  • Series::index_put_: the in-place sibling.

  • Series::put_: flat write semantics.

  • Series::extract_put: selector-language copy-returning writes.
